newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF FRENCH OPEN WOMEN'S FINALISTS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF FRENCH OPEN WOMEN'S FINALISTS.

text.p: Portraits of Martina Hingis and Iva Majoli, who will contest the French Open women's final on Saturday:

Already threatening to end the Graf/Seles era in women's tennis after becoming the youngest grand slam champion in the Open era by beating France's Mary Pierce in the Australian Open final in January. Top of the world rankings, she is unbeaten in 37 matches this year. Despite her slender frame she is capable of surprising power from the baseline but it is her timing and calm, unflustered demeanour under pressure which mark her out as something special. Also appears to enjoy herself on court far more than most of her rivals.
Seeding: 1. Age: 16. Plays right-handed. Weight: 53 kg. Height: 1.67m. Ranking: 1. Tournament wins: 8 (including 1997 Australian Open). Career prize money: $2.78 million.

Bears physical resemblance to Monica Seles but, having made her grand slam debut at the age of 15 in 1992, has endured a long wait to reach her first grand slam final. Has already won two titles this year in Hanover and Hamburg and will rise to fifth in the world after this tournament. Energetic player usually to be found on the baseline, she is another of the clutch of younger players starting to emerge from the shadow of Graf and Seles.
Seeding: 9. Age: 19. Plays right-handed (two-handed backhand). Weight: 61 kg. Height: 1.73m. Ranking: 9. Tournament wins: 6. Career prize money: $2.26 million.
